thread:
billing-alert-bot: ALERT: Multiple customers flagged for unexpected overages and delayed usage ingestion. Metric: token_count vs invoice_tokens diverging. Triggered by rule: metering.delta_rate(5m) > 2000. Affected regions: us-west-2, eu-central.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-METER-DRIFT. Priority: P2. Paging oncall. Runbook: /runbooks/metering/token-drift.md

Alex (oncall): grabbing this. saw a spike in token_count for a subset of tenants ~09:10. Are we seeing delayed ingestion or double-counting?

Maria R: I just checked raw events in kafka: partition 12 shows a replayed window from 08:50-09:05, duplicate keys present. Could be producer retries + new dedupe logic not applied. Query I ran: `select tenant_id, count(*) as c from metering.events where ts between '2026-03-15T08:45Z' and '2026-03-15T09:15Z' group by tenant_id order by c desc limit 20;`

Tim L: confirming. The ingest service returned 500s for a brief period at 08:52 which triggered retries. New dedupe middleware was toggled last week; I wonder if edge case exists when `req_id` is absent.

Jess (billing): customers are getting overage flags in the console and some automated overage emails were sent. We need to stop outbound billing notifications until we understand scope. Can we pause the notifier?

Alex (oncall): Action list: 1) Pause billing-notifier (Jess) 2) Flip metering to safe-mode (dedupe-by-hash enabled) (Tim) 3) Start background job to reconcile token counts for impacted tenants (Maria + Dmitri) 4) Notify CS to hold outbound comms (Oliver). I'll assign tasks and do handoff at +30m.

Dmitri (sre): starting reconciliation plan. We'll compute `expected_tokens = invoice_tokens_before + new_ingested - duplicates` and diff per tenant. Running a small dry-run against staging snapshot. Command: `python scripts/reconcile_tokens.py --snapshot s3://snapshots/metering/2026-03-15-08 --tenants-file /tmp/tenants.txt`

eng-platform-bot: Note: a recent deploy 2026-03-10 changed metering dedupe key precedence order. See PR #4032.

Maria R: I pulled sample events; duplicates have identical client_nonce but different request_id header. Dedupe-by-hash would catch them; current live router prefers request_id when present, so it's letting duplicates through.

Tim L: I'm going to roll back the router flag to prefer hash-based dedupe for now. Planning a config roll with canary 10%. Will monitor ingestion backlog.

Alex (oncall): Good. Jess, can you pause notifier? If you don't have a kill-switch, we can cut the notifier queue (rabbitmq pause) for a maintenance window.

Jess (billing): Pausing queue now: `rabbitmqctl set_policy pause-notifier "^billing-notifier.*" '{}' --apply-to queues` — pausing. Confirmed: queue consumers drained but messages will not be produced. :white_check_mark:

Oliver (cs): Preparing a templated customer message: short note that we're investigating billing anomalies and will not take action until reconciled. Do not promise credits yet, just transparency.

Tim L: Canary rollback started at 09:36. Canary looks good, dedupe rate dropped on canary nodes. Patching global config at 09:44.

Dmitri (sre): Kickoff reconciliation at 09:50. Estimated affected tenant count ~1.2k, concentrated in older orgs. Running reconciliation in batches to avoid throttling billing DB.

Alex (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline for lunch at 10:10, Tim will take primary for incident. Tim, if this escalates to P1 (widespread billing inaccuracies) page myself and the SRE lead.

Tim L: Taking over. I'll keep the incident channel updated every 15m. Next update in 15.

(15m later)

Tim L: Update 10:30 — dedupe rollback looks stable, duplicates dropping to baseline. Reconciliation phase 1: 300 tenants processed, 78 with >5% token delta. Holding writeback until QA signoff.

Maria R: Reconcile script found that the metering pipeline reprocessed a window due to consumer group offset reset at 08:52. Offsets were reset by an automated task that attempted to handle a high-latency consumer. Adding that to root cause notes.

Jess (billing): We've suppressed all outbound billing triggers. No further overage emails sent after 09:12. Existing flagged UI badges are still visible — we should add a temporary banner explaining "Investigating billing display issues".

Oliver (cs): Draft banner posted to #marketing-drafts for review. Also preparing an FAQ for impacted customers.

Dmitri (sre): Preliminary mitigation: 1) Stop writeback to billing ledger for affected tenants (safety) 2) Mark affected tenants as "billing_review" in internal DB 3) Schedule manual crediting assessment after reconciliation.

Alex (oncall): A couple of asks for the post-incident: - Full timeline (deploys, offset reset, retries) - List of tenants and final token deltas - Customer-facing note + approval - Root cause and fix PRs (eg: fix for automated offset reset logic, config for dedupe precedence)

Tim L: Logging an incident task list in INC-2026-0315 ticket and assigning owners. I'll keep the channel updated. Pulled logs and will attach to the incident doc.

(1h later)

Tim L: 11:10 final update for this thread: dedupe fix rolled globally, reconciliation finished for high-priority tenants. No P1 escalation required. Billing UI flags will be recalculated overnight; notifier remains paused until final reconciliation completed. We'll run a dry-run of invoice regeneration and manual QA tomorrow morning.

Alex (oncall): Thanks everyone. Handing back to oncall rotation. Closing live coordination thread; incident remains in monitoring. Postmortem to be written by Tim + Maria with contribs from SRE and Billing.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-METER-DRIFT status -> monitoring. Postmortem owner assigned: Tim L. Due date: 2026-03-22.

Oliver (cs): I'll follow up with CS notes and a customer template for tomorrow.

Jess (billing): Leaving a TODO to run the invoice regen smoke: `./tools/regenerate_invoices --tenants-file /tmp/priority_tenants.txt --dry-run`

Tim L: End of thread. Thanks all. :pray:"
